monthly_review.summary: You've shifted toward higher-intensity running this month, with significantly more time in Zones 4 and 5, but at the cost of reduced volume and aerobic base maintenance.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone 4 time jumped from 15% to 35% while Zone 1+2 dropped from 53% to 28%, indicating a sharp shift away from foundational aerobic work.

goal_tracker.message: You need 39.6 more km across 7 sessions in the remaining 24 days — averaging ~5.7 km per run — to match last month’s volume.

insights.title: Efficiency improved despite lower cadence
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.46 to 13.9 m/km per spm even as average cadence fell from 151 to 148 spm — suggesting gains in stride length (e.g., 75.77 cm on 7/1 vs 72.2 cm on 6/28) and/or reduced ground contact time (311 ms → 305 ms on long run), likely reflecting neuromuscular adaptation under higher load.

insights.title: Over-reliance on Zone 4
insights.body: Zone 4 now accounts for 35% of total HR time — up from 15% last month — while Zone 1+2 collapsed from 53% to 28%, eroding aerobic base development and increasing fatigue risk without compensatory recovery runs.

insights.title: Stride length increased, vertical oscillation stable
insights.body: Stride length rose from 72.2 cm (6/28) to 75.77 cm (7/1) and 75.73 cm (7/5), while vertical oscillation remained tightly clustered between 7.6–8.5 cm — indicating efficient power transfer without wasted bounce, especially during the 10 km run at 8:27/km pace and 166 bpm.

insights.title: Insufficient low-HR recovery
insights.body: Only one recent run (7/8, 4.0 km at 129 bpm, 8:32/km) fell clearly into Zone 1 (<132 bpm); the other four averaged ≥148 bpm — meaning just 1 of 5 recent runs served true recovery function, despite elevated aerobic TE (4.0) on the 10 km.

recommendations.action: Do your next run as a strict Zone 1–2 aerobic recovery session: 6 km at avg HR ≤135 bpm and pace ≥8:50/km (≥530 sec/km).
recommendations.reason: Only 1 of your last 5 runs was truly recovery-focused; your current Zone 1+2 share (28%) is well below the 50–60% ideal for sustainable aerobic development.

recommendations.action: Insert a 30-min easy run (Zone 1–2) within 48 hours of your next Zone 4 session to restore HR zone balance.
recommendations.reason: Your July Zone 4 volume (35%) is unsustainable without adequate recovery stimulus — Garmin’s aerobic TE of 4.0 on 7/5 signals high stress requiring offsetting low-intensity work.

recommendations.action: Perform cadence drills before your next 5 km run: 3 × 1 min @ 156 spm (metronome), focusing on quick turnover and light footstrike, then maintain ≥152 spm for the full run.
recommendations.reason: Cadence declined from 151 (June) to 148 (July), and your most efficient strides occurred at 153–154 spm — targeting 152+ will support efficiency gains without overstriding.

weekly_focus.description: Restore Zone 1–2 volume to rebuild endurance resilience and offset recent high-intensity emphasis — prioritizing time-in-zone over pace or distance.
